svg.text: cut on the cross centre-line, so the slot reads full depth
section at z = 0.30, just above the lead-in chamfer
The display-seat floor, looking down +Z. The second
stamp is the same, mirrored, in the pocket ceiling, and
reads correctly from below (V4). Thin outline = the
seat floor, i.e. the face the stamp is cut into.
click tab 3x, centred on the edge -- 0.40 wide, 0.30 tall, 0.20 proud (note 10)
cap tilt 7° about X (the S profile)
1. Dimensions in mm. First-angle projection (ISO 128). Scale as marked per view.
Axes are the model's own (OpenSCAD): +X right, +Y back, +Z up, origin at the centre of
the MX stem on the moulding face (z = 0). Each view carries the pair it shows.
2. General tolerance ISO 2768-m; ±0.10 applies to the dimensions shown here.
3. Geometry re-authored from keycap_stem.scad in build123d. The STEP is the shape reference;
THIS DRAWING governs tolerance, material and finish.
4. CRITICAL MX slot 4.05 x 1.10 ±0.03, R0.30 corner fillets (V7). Gauge against a real MX
switch stem, not by CMM alone. See the fit table -- our slot is deliberately tighter than
Cherry's published keycap slot, and the four relief bulges are what make that work.
5. CRITICAL The transparent relegendable cap is an off-the-shelf POS part, so that mating
dimension is a hard datum set by a supplier we do not control. Confirm before cutting steel.
6. Draft, measured off the model: outer body 11.6°, inside pocket 18.4°.
7. ZERO DRAFT on the display seat (12.2 x 12.1 x 1.1 deep) and its cable relief. Shallow
enough that it usually releases, but confirm it rather than meet it at first article.
8. The inner chamfer in V4 (33.0°) is switch-body clearance, not cosmetic -- it is what stops
the cap fouling a bulky switch. Do not flatten it to simplify the core.
9. Slot draft 0.08° on the flats, 0.31° at the arm tips, opening downward: the core pin
withdraws in the correct direction, but with very little relief. Polish along the arms.
10. The three 0.40 x 3.00 x 0.30 tabs standing 0.20 proud (+Y and ±X, V3) are a FUNCTIONAL
feature: they are what makes the clear keycap click on properly. They are NOT a
3D-printing artefact and must NOT be removed.
11. Stamp "β S" = revision + profile, 0.30 deep, zero draft, in two places (V8).
Revision character is U+03B2 GREEK SMALL LETTER BETA -- the moulded part is
deliberately β where the 3D-printed prototypes are α, so the two are told apart by eye.
Carry it on a REPLACEABLE INSERT in the cavity rather than cut into the block: a revision
change is then a plug swap, not a tool edit. Font Noto Sans Bold, outlines in the STEP.
12. The slot lead-in opens to 4.61 x 4.61 at z = 0 over 0.30 mm (~46°). Cherry publishes no
lead-in dimension, so this one is ours; keep it, it is what lets the cap start on the stem.
13. MATERIAL ABS, chosen for shrink: 0.4-0.7 % is what keeps the slot inside note 4.
Dimensions are the FINISHED PART -- apply shrink to the cavity and state the rate used.
14. Surface: tool polish on the slot and the stem bore; the outer faces may carry the standard
texture. No flash permitted on the slot, the tabs or the seat floor.
MX SLOT vs CHERRY'S PUBLISHED KEYCAP SPEC
Sources: Cherry's keycap slot spec via deskthority / telcontar.net. The stem's own cross is
ASYMMETRIC and Cherry's uniform 1.17 slot already interferes ~0.07 on two sides; ours is
tighter still, so the fit rests on the relief bulges. Verify on a moulded first article.
